To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency and effectiveness in undergraduate higher education are related to the expenditures, and the optimal expenditure level is $8,500 per student.

(1) institutions with higher expenditures are more effective, but only up to a point; (2) the optimal expenditure level is $9,400 per student, and (3) institutions with higher efficiencies are more effective, and this relationship is stronger at lower expenditure levels.

(1) there is a relationship between an institution's expenditure level and its efficiency, (2) there is a positive relationship between an institution' expenditure level and its effectiveness, and (3) there is a point of diminishing marginal returns for an institution's effectiveness as its expenditures increase beyond a certain level.
